subject: law
intro: Law leads to paid work applying and adjudicating rules — arguing cases in court, deciding them from the bench, researching and preparing them behind the scenes, or settling them without a hearing at all.

roles.title: Lawyers
roles.what: Represent clients in criminal and civil litigation and other legal proceedings, draw up legal documents, and manage or advise on legal transactions — specialising across areas from crime to contract.
roles.where: The criminal law, tort and contract units teach the substantive doctrines lawyers argue daily, while the law-making and English-legal-system unit explains the courts and precedents they practise in.

roles.title: Judges, Magistrate Judges, and Magistrates
roles.what: Arbitrate, advise, adjudicate and administer justice in courts of law — determining liability in civil cases and sentencing defendants in criminal cases according to statutes and sentencing guidelines.
roles.where: The nature-of-law unit — law and morality, law and justice, the rule of law — is exactly the framework judges apply when weighing cases; criminal law and tort supply the offences and liabilities they adjudicate.

roles.title: Paralegals and Legal Assistants
roles.what: Assist lawyers by investigating facts, preparing legal documents and researching legal precedent — building the evidence and argument files that support legal proceedings, defences and claims.
roles.where: The legal-system unit's law-making process and court structure teach where precedent lives and how to read it; the contract unit's essential requirements and statutory terms are the documents paralegals draft and check.

roles.title: Arbitrators, Mediators, and Conciliators
roles.what: Facilitate negotiation and conflict resolution through dialogue, resolving disputes outside the court system by the mutual consent of the parties involved.
roles.where: Contract law — offer, acceptance and enforceable terms — is the body of rules most mediated disputes turn on, and the syllabus's law-and-justice discussions train the fairness reasoning arbitration demands.
